report_markdown:
# AEO/GEO audit: example.com
2026-10-12 · Overall **70/100** — Ready to be cited, but nothing outside the site corroborates it.

| Category | Score | Finding |
|---|---|---|
| AI crawler access | 9/10 | robots.txt allows all agents (`User-agent: *` / `Allow: /`) and declares the sitemap. |
| llms.txt | 8/10 | Present and well-formed; links the FAQ and About pages, but not the blog. |
| Answerability | 9/10 | Quotable definition up top; question headings; nine FAQ pairs. |
| Metadata | 7/10 | Titles are specific on every page audited; descriptions and structured data not visible in the extracted text. |
| External authority | 3/10 | Search returned only the brand's own pages. |
| Depth & freshness | 6/10 | Solid core pages; one dated post (2026-03-02) and a launch post. |

## Strengths
- Quotable definition: "Example Ledger is bookkeeping software for independent cafes and bakeries."
- robots.txt allows every crawler and declares https://example.com/sitemap.xml.
- llms.txt present, with a summary line and described links.
- Nine real question-and-answer pairs on the FAQ.

## Gaps
- No independent coverage: both searches returned only example.com pages.
- The site does not appear for the buyer question except through its own launch post.
- Meta descriptions and structured data could not be checked from rendered text.

## Fix first (ranked)
1. Earn independent coverage: reviews, directory listings, a guest post on a cafe-trade site (project).
2. Publish a comparison page answering "best bookkeeping software for a small cafe" (project).
3. Add the blog to llms.txt (quick fix).

## What this audit could not verify
- Meta descriptions, canonical tags and JSON-LD: not exposed in the extracted text.

## Sources
- https://example.com/ · https://example.com/robots.txt · https://example.com/llms.txt · https://example.com/faq · https://example.com/about · https://example.com/blog/launch
